### `private_todo_app_todos`

User's private todo items with title, description, dates, completion
status, and soft-delete support for trash functionality.

Each todo belongs to a single member and contains the task details
including a required title, optional description, optional start and due
dates, and completion status. Todos support soft deletion through the
deleted_at field, enabling trash functionality where users can view
deleted todos, restore them, or permanently delete them.

When a todo is permanently deleted (removed from trash), its associated
edit history entries are cascade deleted. Todos are completely private -
each member can only access their own todos.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to [private_todo_app_members](#private_todo_app_members) via user_id
- Has many [private_todo_app_todo_edit_histories](#private_todo_app_todo_edit_histories) tracking all
modifications

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_id`: Owner of this todo. References [private_todo_app_members.id](#private_todo_app_members).
- `title`
  > Title of the todo item. Required field that provides a brief summary of
  > the task.
- `description`
  > Detailed description of the todo item. Optional field for additional
  > context or notes about the task.
- `start_date`
  > Optional start date for the todo item. When sorting by start date, todos
  > without a start date appear at the end.
- `due_date`
  > Optional due date for the todo item. When sorting by due date, todos
  > without a due date appear at the end.
- `completed`
  > Completion status of the todo. Newly created todos are incomplete (false)
  > by default. Users can toggle between complete and incomplete states.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was created. Used for sorting todos by creation
  > date.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was last modified. Updated on every edit
  > operation.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp. When set, the todo is in the trash and excluded
  > from normal todo lists. Null for active todos.

### `private_todo_app_todo_edit_histories`

Edit history entries that track field-level changes made to todos over time.

Each history entry captures a single edit event, recording the timestamp
when the modification occurred and documenting which specific fields were
altered during that change. Only fields that were actually modified
during the edit are recorded; unchanged fields remain null in that entry.

This table serves as an audit trail for todo modifications, allowing
users to review the complete evolution of their todo items. History
entries are automatically created whenever a todo's title, description,
start date, or due date is modified, and are permanently deleted when the
parent todo is permanently removed from the trash.

Relationships:
- Belongs to [private_todo_app_todos](#private_todo_app_todos) via private_todo_app_todo_id
- Cascade deleted when parent todo is permanently deleted

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `private_todo_app_todo_id`: Reference to the todo that was edited. [private_todo_app_todos.id](#private_todo_app_todos).
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this edit was made. Used for sorting history entries from
  > most recent to oldest.
- `title`
  > The new title value after the edit, if the todo's title was modified
  > during this change. Null if the title was not changed.
- `description`
  > The new description value after the edit, if the todo's description was
  > modified during this change. Null if the description was not changed.
- `start_date`
  > The new start date value after the edit, if the todo's start date was
  > modified during this change. Null if the start date was not changed.
- `due_date`
  > The new due date value after the edit, if the todo's due date was
  > modified during this change. Null if the due date was not changed.

# Multi-User Todo Application

I want to create a multi-user Todo list application.

## User Account

- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- Users can delete their account (all their todos, including those in trash, are permanently deleted)

## User Profile

- Each user has a profile with: display name
- Users can edit their display name
- Users cannot view other users' profiles (this is a private todo app)

## Creating Todos

- Users can create a todo with:
  - Title (required)
  - Description (optional, can be left empty)
  - Start date (optional, can be left empty)
  - Due date (optional, can be left empty)
- Newly created todos are incomplete by default

## Viewing Todos

- Users can view a list of their own todos
- The list is paginated
- Each todo in the list shows: title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation date
- Users can view a single todo to see all its details including full description

## Completing Todos

- Users can mark a todo as complete
- Users can mark a todo as incomplete
- This is a simple toggle between two states

## Editing Todos

- Users can edit their todo's title, description, start date, and due date
- Every edit is recorded in the todo's history

## Edit History

- Each todo has an edit history
- Every time a todo is edited, a history entry is created
- Each history entry records:
  - When the edit was made
  - What the title was changed to (if changed)
  - What the description was changed to (if changed)
  - What the start date was changed to (if changed)
  - What the due date was changed to (if changed)
- Users can view the full edit history of any of their todos
- History entries are sorted from most recent to oldest

## Deleting Todos

- Users can delete their own todos
- Deleted todos are not permanently removed (soft delete)
- Deleted todos no longer appear in the normal todo list

## Trash

- Users can view a list of their deleted todos (trash)
- The trash list is paginated
- Users can restore a deleted todo from the trash (it returns to the normal todo list)
- Users can permanently delete a todo from the trash
- Permanently deleting a todo also deletes its edit history

## Filtering Todos

- Users can filter their todo list by completion status:
  - All todos
  - Only complete todos
  - Only incomplete todos

## Sorting Todos

- Users can sort their todo list by:
  - Creation date (newest first or oldest first)
  - Start date (earliest first or latest first)
  - Due date (earliest first or latest first)
- Todos without a start date appear at the end when sorting by start date
- Todos without a due date appear at the end when sorting by due date

## Privacy

- Each user's todos are completely private
- Users can only see their own todos
- There is no way to view, access, or share another user's todos

operations.specification:
Implementation of guest join operation for new user registration.

**Service Layer Logic:**
1. Validate the request body containing email and password
2. Check if email already exists in the member table (prevent duplicate accounts)
3. Hash the password using secure hashing algorithm (bcrypt/argon2)
4. Create a new member record with email and hashed password
5. Generate JWT access token and refresh token for the new member
6. Optionally link the current guest session to the new member for analytics

**Database Operations:**
- Read: Check member table for existing email
- Write: Create new member record
- Write: Create member session record

**Business Rules:**
- Email must be unique across all members
- Password must meet minimum security requirements (length, complexity)
- Access token expires in 2 hours, refresh token in 14 days

**Error Handling:**
- 400: Invalid email format or password requirements not met
- 409: Email already exists in system
- 500: Database or internal errors
operations.description:
Enables unauthenticated guests to sign up for a new member account in the private todo application.

This operation is the primary entry point for new users joining the application. Guests provide their email address and password credentials to create a new member account. Upon successful registration, the system creates a new member record and returns authentication tokens (access token and refresh token) that establish an authenticated session.

The email address must be unique across the system - if the email is already registered, the operation fails with a conflict error. The password must meet the system's security requirements including minimum length and complexity standards.

Once the join operation succeeds, the guest transitions from an unauthenticated state to an authenticated member state with full access to their personal todo features including creating, viewing, editing, completing, and deleting todos.

The response includes both an access token (short-lived, for API authentication) and a refresh token (long-lived, for token renewal), enabling the new member to maintain their authenticated session.

requestBody.description: Guest join request containing email and password for new account registration.

responseBody.description: Authorized response containing access token and refresh token for the newly created member account.

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
Implementation of guest session token refresh operation.

**Service Layer Logic:**
1. Extract and validate the refresh token from the request body
2. Verify the refresh token signature and expiration
3. Check if the refresh token exists in the session store and is not revoked
4. Retrieve the associated guest record from the database
5. Generate new access token and refresh token pair
6. Optionally revoke the old refresh token (rotation for security)
7. Store the new refresh token in the session store

**Database Operations:**
- Read: Query guest_sessions table by refresh token
- Read: Query guests table for guest record
- Write: Update session record with new refresh token

**Business Rules:**
- Refresh token must be valid and not expired
- Refresh token must not be revoked or previously used
- New access token expires in 2 hours
- New refresh token expires in 14 days

**Error Handling:**
- 401: Invalid or expired refresh token
- 401: Refresh token has been revoked
- 500: Database or internal errors
operations.description:
Refreshes the guest session tokens to maintain an active session state.

This operation allows guests to renew their session tokens without re-authenticating. The client provides a valid refresh token, and the server responds with a new access token and refresh token pair.

The refresh mechanism is essential for maintaining continuous guest session tracking without requiring the visitor to re-authenticate frequently. This supports the analytics and session tracking features that monitor guest behavior before they sign up or log in.

For security purposes, the refresh token should be rotated - each refresh operation issues a new refresh token and invalidates the previous one. This prevents token replay attacks and enhances session security.

The operation validates that the provided refresh token is still valid, has not expired, and has not been revoked. If any of these checks fail, the operation returns an authentication error, and the guest session ends.

requestBody.description: Guest refresh request containing the current refresh token.

responseBody.description: Authorized response containing new access token and refresh token pair.

operations.name: refresh

Implementation details for member registration:

1. Validate email format and check uniqueness against private_todo_app_members.email unique constraint
2. Hash the provided password using secure one-way hashing algorithm (bcrypt/argon2)
3. Create new record in private_todo_app_members with:

The session data includes creation timestamp (login time) and expiration timestamp for validating JWT token validity and enforcing session timeout policies. Sessions are sorted by creation date (most recent first) by default, making it easy to see recent login activity.

Members can filter sessions by IP address, creation date range, and expiration status. This helps identify suspicious login activity or track session history. All sessions automatically expire based on the expired_at timestamp.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filterable list of the authenticated member's active todos.

This operation provides the main todo list view for members, displaying their personal todo items with essential summary information. Each todo in the response includes its title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation date.

Members can filter todos by completion status to show all items, only completed todos, or only incomplete todos. The list supports sorting by creation date, start date, or due date in ascending or descending order. When sorting by start date or due date, todos without those dates appear at the end of the list.

Pagination is supported for efficient browsing of large todo collections. The response includes both the paginated data and pagination metadata for navigation.

Privacy is strictly enforced: members can only view their own todos, and the main list excludes soft-deleted todos (items in the trash). Use the trash endpoint to view deleted todos.

Security: This endpoint requires member authentication. The user_id filter is automatically applied based on the authenticated member's identity, ensuring complete data isolation between users.

operations.specification:
Query the private_todo_app_todos table with the following constraints:

1. Filter by user_id matching the authenticated member's id
2. Exclude soft-deleted todos (deleted_at IS NULL)
3. Apply completion status filter from request:
   - 'all' or omitted: no completion filter
   - 'complete': completed = true
   - 'incomplete': completed = false
4. Apply optional title search using case-insensitive partial matching with GIN trigram index
5. Apply sorting:
   - 'created_at' with 'desc' (newest first) or 'asc' (oldest first)
   - 'start_date' with 'asc' (earliest first) or 'desc' (latest first) - nulls last
   - 'due_date' with 'asc' (earliest first) or 'desc' (latest first) - nulls last
6. Implement cursor-based or offset-based pagination using request pagination parameters
7. Return total count and page data

Database indexes available for optimization:
- @@index([user_id, completed, deleted_at]) for completion filtering
- @@index([user_id, created_at, deleted_at]) for created_at sorting
- @@index([user_id, start_date, deleted_at]) for start_date sorting
- @@index([user_id, due_date, deleted_at]) for due_date sorting
- GIN trigram index on title for search

Security: Verify authenticated member, filter by user_id to enforce data isolation.

Any attempt to access a todo belonging to another member will result in an access denied response, without revealing whether the todo exists for that other user.

The todo must be an active (non-deleted) todo. Todos that have been soft-deleted and moved to the trash are not accessible through this endpoint; use the trash viewing operations instead.

The following fields can be modified:
- Title: The main summary of the todo task (required)
- Description: Detailed notes or context for the todo (optional)
- Start date: When the task should begin (optional)
- Due date: When the task should be completed by (optional)

Every modification is automatically recorded in the todo's edit history, which tracks when changes were made and what values changed. The edit history can be viewed using the GET /todos/{todoId}/histories endpoint.

This operation cannot update the completion status of a todo - use the dedicated completion toggle operation for that purpose. Deleted todos (those in the trash) cannot be updated and will return a not found response.

- Todo in trash (deleted_at not null): treat as not found

operations.description:
Toggle the completion status of a specific todo item.

This endpoint allows authenticated members to toggle their todo's completion status between complete and incomplete. The toggle is a simple flip operation - if the todo is currently incomplete, it becomes complete; if currently complete, it becomes incomplete.

The operation requires the todo's unique identifier as a path parameter. Only the owner of the todo can toggle its completion status. Attempting to toggle a todo belonging to another user results in an access denied response. If the specified todo does not exist, a not found response is returned.

Upon successful toggle, the updated todo is returned with the new completion status reflected in the 'completed' field and the 'updated_at' timestamp refreshed to reflect the modification time. The completion status can be toggled any number of times without restriction.

This operation references the private_todo_app_todos table, specifically modifying the 'completed' boolean field (which defaults to false for newly created todos) and the 'updated_at' timestamp field. The todo must belong to the authenticated member as determined by the user_id foreign key reference to private_todo_app_members.
operations.name: toggle
operations.specification:
Implement the todo completion toggle as follows:

1. Authentication: Extract member ID from JWT session token. Reject with 401 if unauthenticated.

2. Todo Lookup: Query private_todo_app_todos table by id (UUID) where user_id matches authenticated member's ID.

3. Authorization Checks:
   - If no todo found with matching id AND user_id: Check if todo exists for ANY user
     - If exists for another user: Return 403 Forbidden (access denied)
     - If doesn't exist at all: Return 404 Not Found
   - Security consideration: Do NOT reveal whether a todo exists for another user

4. Toggle Operation:
   - Read current 'completed' field value
   - Flip the boolean: completed = !completed
   - Update 'updated_at' to current timestamp
   - Save changes to database

5. Response: Return the complete updated todo entity including:
   - id, user_id, title, description, start_date, due_date
   - completed (new toggled value)
   - created_at, updated_at (updated timestamp)
   - deleted_at (should be null for active todos)

6. Edge Cases:
   - Todo in trash (deleted_at is not null): Should still be toggleable, respond with updated todo
   - Concurrent requests: Use database transaction to ensure atomicity
   - Invalid UUID format in path: Return 400 Bad Request

responseBody.description: The updated todo with its new completion status and refreshed updated_at timestamp.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo item to toggle. Must be a valid UUID referencing an existing todo owned by the authenticated member.
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created first before its completion status can be toggled

operations.description:
Delete a todo by moving it to the trash.

This operation performs a soft delete on the specified todo, setting the deleted_at timestamp which moves the todo to the user's trash. The todo is not permanently removed from the database and can be restored from the trash at a later time.

The todo's edit history entries are retained during this operation, allowing users to view the complete modification history if the todo is later restored from the trash.

Authorization is strictly enforced - users can only delete their own todos. Attempting to delete a todo belonging to another user will result in a not found response. This ensures complete privacy of each user's todo data without revealing whether a todo exists for another user.

After deletion, the todo will no longer appear in the normal todo list but can be accessed through the trash endpoint where users can view deleted todos, restore them, or permanently delete them.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Set the deleted_at timestamp on the todo record identified by todoId.

Implementation steps:
1. Authenticate the member from the session token
2. Validate todoId is a valid UUID format
3. Query private_todo_app_todos table for record where id = todoId AND user_id = authenticated_member_id AND deleted_at IS NULL
4. If no record found, return 404 not found (todo doesn't exist or doesn't belong to user or already deleted)
5. Update the todo record setting deleted_at = current timestamp and updated_at = current timestamp
6. Do NOT delete associated edit history entries (they are retained for potential restoration)
7. Return the updated todo record with deleted_at populated

Authorization: Only the owning member can delete their todos. Users cannot delete todos belonging to other users.

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized: If user is not authenticated
- 404 Not Found: If todo doesn't exist, doesn't belong to user, or is already deleted
- 400 Bad Request: If todoId is not a valid UUID

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to delete. Must be a valid UUID that corresponds to an existing, non-deleted todo owned by the authenticated user.
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: Todo must exist before it can be deleted. This operation creates the todo and returns its id which becomes the todoId path parameter for the delete operation.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of deleted todos from the trash.

This operation allows authenticated members to view their soft-deleted todos that have been moved to the trash. Each todo in the trash remains accessible for restoration or permanent deletion. The trash provides a safety net for accidentally deleted items, giving users the opportunity to recover them before permanent removal.

The response includes summarized information for each deleted todo: title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation date. Deleted todos remain in the trash until explicitly restored or permanently deleted. The deleted_at timestamp determines when the todo was moved to trash.

Privacy is strictly enforced - members can only view their own deleted todos. The system automatically scopes the query to the authenticated member's user_id, ensuring complete data isolation between users. Any attempt to access another member's trash items will result in an empty result set.

Supports filtering by completion status, date ranges, and title search. Sorting options include creation date, start date, due date, and deletion date. Pagination ensures efficient browsing of large trash collections.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the private_todo_app_todos table with the following filters:

1. Filter by user_id matching the authenticated member's ID
2. Filter by deleted_at IS NOT NULL (only soft-deleted todos)
3. Apply optional search filters from request body:
   - Title partial matching using case-insensitive search
   - Completion status filter (completed/incomplete/all)
   - Date range filters for created_at, start_date, due_date
4. Apply sorting based on request parameters:
   - Default sort by deleted_at descending (most recently deleted first)
   - Support sorting by created_at, start_date, due_date
   - Todos without start_date/due_date appear at the end when sorting by those fields
5. Apply pagination using cursor-based approach:
   - Use created_at or id as cursor for stable pagination
   - Return pagination metadata with next cursor

Database query should use the existing indexes on [user_id, deleted_at] for optimal performance.

Return only todos belonging to the authenticated member to enforce privacy.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of deleted todo summaries from trash

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filters, and pagination parameters for trash items

operations.description:
Restore a deleted todo from the trash back to the active todo list.

This operation moves a soft-deleted todo back to the normal todo list by clearing its deleted_at timestamp. All original todo attributes are preserved during restoration, including title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and complete edit history.

The operation requires the todo to exist in the authenticated user's trash. Only the owner of the todo can restore it - attempting to restore another user's todo will result in an access denied error. If the todo is not found in the trash (either never deleted or already permanently deleted), the request is rejected.

Upon successful restoration, the todo immediately becomes visible in the normal todo list and can be edited, completed, or deleted again. The restoration action is reversible - users can delete the todo again to return it to the trash.

Related operations:
- PATCH /trash lists all deleted todos
- DELETE /trash/{todoId} permanently deletes a todo from trash
- DELETE /todos/{todoId} moves a todo to trash (soft delete)
operations.name: restore
operations.specification:
Implementation logic for todo restoration:

1. Authenticate the member from JWT session token
2. Validate todoId path parameter as valid UUID
3. Query private_todo_app_todos table WHERE id = todoId AND user_id = authenticated_member_id
4. Verify the todo exists and belongs to current user (404 not found if no match)
5. Verify deleted_at IS NOT NULL (todo is in trash) - return error if already active
6. Set deleted_at = NULL via UPDATE query
7. Update updated_at to current timestamp
8. Return the complete restored todo entity

Error handling:
- 404 if todo not found or does not belong to user
- 400 if todo is not in trash (deleted_at is null)
- 401 if not authenticated

Database query:
UPDATE private_todo_app_todos 
SET deleted_at = NULL, updated_at = NOW()
WHERE id = $todoId AND user_id = $memberId AND deleted_at IS NOT NULL
RETURNING *

responseBody.description: The restored todo with all original attributes preserved, now visible in the normal todo list.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to restore from trash. The todo must belong to the authenticated user and must have been soft-deleted (present in trash).
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: Todo must exist before it can be restored from trash. The todoId path parameter references a todo that must have been created by this operation and subsequently soft-deleted.

operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo from the trash.

This operation irreversibly removes a todo that has been previously deleted and moved to the trash. Once permanently deleted, the todo and all its associated edit history entries are completely removed from the database and cannot be recovered.

Security and authorization: Only the owner of a todo can permanently delete it. The system validates that the authenticated member is the owner of the todo before allowing permanent deletion. Attempts to permanently delete another user's todo are rejected with an access denied error.

Pre-conditions: The todo must exist in the trash (deleted_at field must be non-null). If the todo exists but is not in the trash, the request is rejected. If the todo has already been permanently deleted, a not found error is returned.

Cascade deletion: When a todo is permanently deleted, all its edit history entries are automatically removed as well. This ensures complete data cleanup and prevents orphaned history records.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Permanently delete a todo from the trash.

Implementation steps:
1. Extract todoId from path parameter and member from JWT authentication context
2. Query private_todo_app_todos table for the specified todoId
3. Validate existence - return 404 Not Found if todo does not exist
4. Validate ownership - return 403 Forbidden if todo.user_id does not match authenticated member's id
5. Validate trash state - return 400 Bad Request if todo.deleted_at is null (todo is not in trash)
6. Permanently delete the todo record from private_todo_app_todos table
7. Edit history entries in private_todo_app_todo_edit_histories are automatically cascade deleted due to onDelete: Cascade constraint
8. Return the deleted todo entity for confirmation

Error handling:
- 404: Todo not found in database
- 403: Todo belongs to another user (access denied)
- 400: Todo is not in trash (cannot permanently delete non-trashed todo)

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to permanently delete from the trash
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before it can be moved to trash and permanently deleted. The todo will be created in active state and must be deleted (moved to trash) by a separate non-POST operation before this permanent deletion can succeed.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of edit history entries for a specific todo item.

This operation allows authenticated users to view the complete modification history of their own todos. Each history entry captures a single edit event, recording when the modification occurred and which specific fields were altered during that change. Only fields that were actually modified are recorded; unchanged fields remain null in that entry.

The history serves as an audit trail for todo modifications, enabling users to review the complete evolution of their todo items over time. History entries are automatically created whenever a todo's title, description, start date, or due date is modified through the edit operation.

Privacy is strictly enforced: users can only view edit history for todos they own. Attempts to access another user's todo history will be rejected. The todo must exist and belong to the authenticated user; otherwise, an appropriate error response is returned.

Results are sorted in reverse chronological order by edit time, with the most recent edits appearing first. This allows users to quickly see the latest changes made to their todo items.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query private_todo_app_todo_edit_histories table filtered by private_todo_app_todo_id matching the path parameter. Join with private_todo_app_todos to verify ownership via user_id matching the authenticated member. Apply pagination using cursor or offset-based approach. Sort results by created_at in descending order (most recent first). Return only history entries for todos not permanently deleted (todos with deleted_at in trash are still viewable for history). Reject access if todo does not belong to authenticated user or does not exist. Each history entry includes: id, created_at, and the changed fields (title, description, start_date, due_date) with their new values.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of edit history entries sorted by most recent first

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo whose edit history is being retrieved. The authenticated user must own this todo.
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Pagination parameters for the edit history list

prerequisites.description: Todo must exist before its edit history can be retrieved. The authenticated member must own the todo, which is established when creating it via this endpoint.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific edit history entry for one of your todos.

This endpoint returns detailed information about a single edit event recorded in the todo's history. Each edit history entry captures the timestamp when the modification occurred and documents which specific fields were altered during that change. Only fields that were actually modified during the edit are recorded; unchanged fields remain null in that entry.

The edit history serves as an audit trail for todo modifications, allowing you to review how your todo has evolved over time. History entries are automatically created whenever a todo's title, description, start date, or due date is modified.

Security and Privacy:
- You can only view edit history for todos you own
- Attempting to access edit history for another user's todo will result in an access denied response
- The system does not reveal whether a todo exists for another user when access is denied

Related Operations:
- Use GET /todos/{todoId}/editHistories to list all edit history entries for a todo
- Edit history entries are read-only and cannot be modified or deleted individually
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve a specific edit history entry for a todo owned by the authenticated member.

Implementation steps:
1. Extract todoId and editHistoryId from path parameters
2. Query private_todo_app_todos to verify the todo exists and belongs to the authenticated member (user_id matches)
3. If todo not found or not owned by member, return access denied error
4. Query private_todo_app_todo_edit_histories for the entry matching both private_todo_app_todo_id and id
5. If edit history entry not found, return not found error
6. Return the full edit history entry with all fields

Security checks:
- Verify todo ownership before allowing access to edit history
- Do not reveal whether todo exists for other users

Error handling:
- 404 if edit history not found
- 403 if todo belongs to another user (treat as not found to maintain privacy)
- 401 if unauthenticated

responseBody.description: The edit history entry with timestamp and field change details

parameters.description: ID of the todo whose edit history entry to retrieve
parameters.name: todoId

parameters.description: ID of the specific edit history entry to retrieve
parameters.name: editHistoryId

prerequisites.description: Todo must exist before viewing its edit history entries. The edit history belongs to the parent todo via foreign key relationship.

The token object contains access/refresh JWT strings generated server-side using member_id in the payload; tokens are not stored as-is but sessions are tracked in private_todo_app_member_sessions table for validation and revocation.

email.description: Member's email address used for login identification. Must match the email registered during account creation.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to private_todo_app_members.email. Used as unique identifier to lookup member record for authentication. Must be unique across all members (enforced by unique index).

password.description: Member's password for authentication. Verified against the securely stored password hash during login.
password.x-autobe-specification: Maps to private_todo_app_members.password_hash with transformation. User provides plaintext password, which is verified against stored password_hash using secure comparison (e.g., bcrypt.compare) to prevent timing attacks. Password is never stored or transmitted in plaintext.

href.description: The URL where the login request was initiated. Captured for security auditing and session management.
href.x-autobe-specification: Session context field stored in private_todo_app_member_sessions.href upon successful authentication, not in members table. Captures the URL where the login request originated for security auditing. Required field for session tracking.

referrer.description: The referring URL that led to the login page. Used for security auditing and tracking login sources.
referrer.x-autobe-specification: Session context field stored in private_todo_app_member_sessions.referrer upon successful authentication, not in members table. Captures the referring URL for security auditing and fraud detection. Required field for session tracking.

ip.description: Client's IP address for security auditing. Optional field - if not provided, the server will capture the IP from the request context.
ip.x-autobe-specification: Session context field stored in private_todo_app_member_sessions.ip upon successful authentication, not in members table. Optional because in SSR (Server Side Rendering) environments, the client cannot determine its own IP address - the server captures it as fallback (body.ip ?? serverIp). When provided, must be valid IPv4 format.

IPrivateTodoAppMember.ILogin.description: Login credentials for member authentication with email and password. Includes session context fields (href, referrer, ip) for security auditing. Upon successful authentication, a new session is created and JWT tokens are returned in the response.
IPrivateTodoAppMember.ILogin.x-autobe-specification: Login request DTO for member authentication. Email serves as unique identifier for member lookup via unique index on private_todo_app_members.email. Password is verified against password_hash using secure comparison to prevent timing attacks. Session context fields (href, referrer, ip) are captured for security auditing and stored in private_todo_app_member_sessions table upon successful authentication, not in the members table. Upon successful verification, a new session record is created with connection metadata, and JWT tokens are generated for the response.

email.description: Unique email address for member identification and login authentication. Must be unique across all registered members.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to private_todo_app_members.email column. Unique constraint enforced at database level. Backend validates email format and uniqueness before insertion.

password.description: Plain text password for member authentication. Will be securely hashed using one-way cryptographic algorithm before storage in the database.
password.x-autobe-specification: Transformed input: plain text password received from client is hashed using secure one-way algorithm (bcrypt/argon2) and stored in private_todo_app_members.password_hash column.

href.description: Current page URL where the registration request originated. Used for session tracking and security auditing.
href.x-autobe-specification: Cross-table mapping: stored in private_todo_app_member_sessions.href when session is created during registration. Captures the current page URL for security auditing and session tracking. Backend extracts from request context.

referrer.description: Referrer URL that linked to the registration page. Used for session tracking and security auditing.
referrer.x-autobe-specification: Cross-table mapping: stored in private_todo_app_member_sessions.referrer when session is created during registration. Captures the referring URL for security auditing and session tracking. Backend extracts from request context.

ip.description: Client IP address for security auditing. Optional for SSR cases where IP cannot be determined from the client side.
ip.x-autobe-specification: Cross-table mapping: stored in private_todo_app_member_sessions.ip when session is created during registration. Optional because SSR clients cannot determine their own IP - backend falls back to server-detected IP. Nullable field in session table.

IPrivateTodoAppMember.IJoin.description: Request body for member registration containing email, password credentials, and session context information for security tracking. Email must be unique across all members. Password is securely hashed before storage. Session context (current page URL, referrer URL, and optional IP address) is recorded for security auditing.
IPrivateTodoAppMember.IJoin.x-autobe-specification: Request body for member registration. Email validates uniqueness and maps to private_todo_app_members.email. Password is hashed server-side and stored in private_todo_app_members.password_hash - not a direct column mapping. Session context (href, referrer, ip) is captured and stored in private_todo_app_member_sessions for security auditing. Display name intentionally excluded from registration - set to null initially, can be updated via profile endpoint.

id.description: Unique identifier for the authenticated guest.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from private_todo_app_guests.id. UUID primary key identifying the guest.

token.x-autobe-specification: Authorization token comes from the session table.

IPrivateTodoAppGuest.IAuthorized.description: Authorization response for guest session operations. Contains the guest's unique identifier and JWT authentication tokens for maintaining an authenticated session state.
IPrivateTodoAppGuest.IAuthorized.x-autobe-specification: Maps to private_todo_app_guests.id for guest identification. Token object is computed from the associated guest session record in private_todo_app_guest_sessions, containing: access (JWT for API calls, 2-hour expiry), refresh (token for renewal, 14-day expiry), expired_at (access token expiration), and refreshable_until (absolute session deadline). Internal timestamps (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) and the sessions relation are excluded from the response.

id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from private_todo_app_members.id. UUID primary key used for unique member identification.

displayName.description: Display name of the member. Can be null if not set.
displayName.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from private_todo_app_members.display_name. Nullable String column - returns null if member has not set a display name.

IPrivateTodoAppMember.ISummary.description: Lightweight member summary containing essential identification and display information. Used in session and todo contexts to represent the owning member without exposing sensitive credentials or detailed profile data.
IPrivateTodoAppMember.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from private_todo_app_members table for lightweight member summary. id maps to members.id (UUID primary key). displayName maps to members.display_name (nullable String column). Query by id using primary key lookup. Privacy enforcement: summary only exposed when referencing member in their own sessions/todos context - never for other members' data.

scenario.draft:
Test successful guest session token refresh.

Setup: Create initial guest session via join endpoint to obtain a valid refresh token.

Execution: Call refresh endpoint with the valid refresh token from the setup.

Validation:
- Response contains new access token (non-empty string)
- Response contains new refresh token (non-empty string)
- Response includes expired_at timestamp (access token expiration, ~2 hours)
- Response includes refreshable_until timestamp (session deadline, ~14 days)
- New access token expires_at should be approximately 2 hours in the future
- New refresh token's refreshable_until should extend session lifetime
- Verify token rotation: the old refresh token should now be invalid if used again
- Response id matches the guest id from setup
- Token structure matches IAuthorizationToken schema

scenario.draft:
Test guest refresh operation with an expired refresh token.

Execution: Simulate an expired refresh token scenario by either:
- Using a refresh token whose refreshable_until deadline has passed
- Waiting for the token to expire (if time permits in test environment)
- Using a manually crafted expired token for testing

Call refresh endpoint with the expired refresh token.

Validation:
- Response returns 401 Unauthorized status
- Error message indicates the refresh token has expired
- System does not issue new tokens
- Guest session remains terminated (cannot re-authenticate with expired token)
- User would need to start a new session via join operation

scenario.draft:
Test guest refresh operation with a revoked (previously used) refresh token.

Setup: Create initial guest session via join endpoint to obtain a valid refresh token.
Then successfully use that refresh token once, which revokes it due to token rotation security.

Execution: Attempt to use the same (now revoked) refresh token a second time.

Validation:
- Response returns 401 Unauthorized status
- Error message indicates the refresh token has been revoked or is no longer valid
- System prevents token replay attacks by rejecting previously used tokens
- Each refresh token can only be used once (one-time use policy)
- After revocation, only the most recently issued refresh token is valid
- This security measure prevents session hijacking via stolen refresh tokens

- Response status is 200 OK

Test that a member can filter their sessions by active/expired status to distinguish current login sessions from historical ones.

**Test Flow:**
1. Register a new member account via POST /privateTodoApp/auth/member/join
2. Call PATCH /privateTodoApp/member/sessions with request body { is_active: true }
3. Validate the response contains only active sessions (sessions where expired_at > current time)
4. Verify each returned session has expired_at in the future
5. Call PATCH /privateTodoApp/member/sessions with request body { is_active: false }
6. Validate the response contains only expired sessions (sessions where expired_at <= current time)
7. Verify each returned session has expired_at in the past or equal to current time

**Validation Points:**
- Response status is 200 OK for both filter queries
- Active filter returns sessions not yet expired
- Expired filter returns sessions that have already expired
- Pagination metadata correctly reflects the filtered count
- The is_active filter correctly computes session status by comparing expired_at with current timestamp
- Privacy is maintained: only authenticated member's sessions are returned regardless of filter

scenario.draft:
Test that a member can paginate through their session history with custom page size and navigate across multiple pages.

**Test Flow:**
1. Register a new member account via POST /privateTodoApp/auth/member/join
2. Call PATCH /privateTodoApp/member/sessions with request body { page: 1, limit: 10 }
3. Validate the response pagination metadata shows current: 1, limit: 10
4. Verify the data array contains session records (count may be 1 since this is a new account)
5. Call PATCH /privateTodoApp/member/sessions with request body { page: 2, limit: 10 }
6. Validate the response shows current: 2, and data array is empty (no second page of sessions for new account)
7. Test boundary: call with limit: 1 to verify pagination works with minimum page size
8. Validate pagination metadata includes correct total records count and pages count

**Validation Points:**
- Response status is 200 OK for all pagination queries
- Pagination metadata correctly reflects the requested page and limit
- Total pages is calculated correctly as Math.ceil(records / limit)
- Empty pages return empty data array (not error)
- Limit constraint is enforced (maximum 100)
- Privacy is maintained across all paginated results
- Sessions remain sorted by created_at DESC across all pages

scenario.draft:
Test privacy enforcement when a member attempts to access edit history for another member's todo.

Prerequisites:
1. Register Member A via POST /auth/member/join
2. Create a todo as Member A via POST /todos with title 'Member A Task'
3. Update the todo as Member A via PUT /todos/{todoId} to generate edit history
4. List edit history as Member A via PATCH /todos/{todoId}/editHistories to get editHistoryId and todoId
5. Register Member B via POST /auth/member/join (new member with no access to Member A's data)

Test steps:
- As Member B, call GET /todos/{todoId}/editHistories/{editHistoryId} using Member A's todo ID and edit history ID
- Verify the request is rejected with 404 Not Found (not 403, to maintain privacy - system must not reveal whether the todo/edit history exists for another user)
- Verify error response does not indicate whether the todo exists or not
- This enforces the strict privacy boundary where each member's todos and edit history remain completely private
- Verify Member B cannot determine if the todo exists for Member A through any response metadata

Business rule validation:
- Data Access Boundary: Each member can only access todos they created
- Privacy enforcement: No cross-user data access is permitted under any circumstances
- Security: System does not reveal whether a todo exists for another user when access is denied

authorizations.error_analysis: The TypeScript compilation error occurs in src/MyGlobal.ts, not in the authorization components themselves. Error TS2307: Cannot find module './MyConfiguration' or its corresponding type declarations. The authorization files (guestAuthorize.ts, GuestAuth.ts, GuestPayload.ts) are syntactically correct with proper import paths - jwtAuthorize imports from './jwtAuthorize' (same directory), and Payload imports from '../../decorators/payload/GuestPayload'. However, since MyGlobal.ts is a core dependency that the provider imports, the compilation chain fails.
authorizations.solution_guidance: The authorization components (Provider, Decorator, Payload) are correctly implemented. To resolve the compilation error: (1) Create src/MyConfiguration.ts file with proper configuration exports, OR (2) Fix the import path in MyGlobal.ts to point to the correct configuration module location. The auth components use correct patterns: Provider imports jwtAuthorize from './jwtAuthorize', validates payload.type === 'guest', queries private_todo_app_guests with id: payload.id, checks deleted_at: null, and validates session expiration with expired_at: { gt: new Date() }. No changes needed to the authorization component logic.

plan.thinking: IPrivateTodoAppTodo.ICreate is a Create DTO for creating todo items. The x-autobe-database-schema annotation confirms it maps to private_todo_app_todos table. The Create DTO contains title (required), description, start_date, and due_date (optional). The user_id foreign key column is not in the DTO body - it must be extracted from the authenticated member session context. Therefore, references to private_todo_app_members (authorized actor) and private_todo_app_member_sessions (authorized session) are required.

Transformable Read DTO mapping to private_todo_app_member_sessions table. Contains session metadata (id, ip, href, referrer, timestamps) with member relation join to IPrivateTodoAppMember.ISummary. Direct field mappings exist for all columns, and x-autobe-database-schema annotation confirms the table mapping.

Lightweight session summary for paginated listing. Maps to private_todo_app_member_sessions table with member relation JOIN. All fields directly correspond to database columns: id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at. The member field is a nested IPrivateTodoAppMember.ISummary object from JOIN. Transformable DTO for API response.

Transforms private_todo_app_todo_edit_histories to IPrivateTodoAppTodoEditHistory.ISummary. This is a read DTO for API response containing lightweight edit history entry with direct field mappings: id, created_at, title, description, start_date, due_date. Used in paginated history list to show chronological evolution of a todo item, sorted from most recent to oldest.

Transformable DTO - maps to private_todo_app_todos table. Has x-autobe-database-schema annotation confirming table mapping. Properties directly map to DB columns with member relation join to private_todo_app_members.

IPrivateTodoAppMember.ISummary is a lightweight read DTO mapping directly to private_todo_app_members table (id → id, displayName → display_name). It has x-autobe-database-schema annotation confirming the table mapping. Used for API responses in session and todo contexts. Transformable.
